properties.name: management.endpoint.security-rbac.access
properties.description: Permitted level of access for the securityRbac endpoint.

properties.name: management.endpoint.security-rbac.cache.time-to-live
properties.description: Maximum time that a response can be cached.

properties.name: security.rbac.deny-by-default
properties.description: If true (default), a role with no entry in rolePermissions grants NO permissions - fail closed. Setting this false is almost never what you want in a fintech context; it exists for services migrating incrementally from ad-hoc hasRole() checks.

properties.name: security.rbac.role-permissions
properties.description: Role -> granted permissions. This is the actual access policy, expressed as configuration instead of scattered across code - review a diff of this map in a PR and you've reviewed the entire permission change, instead of grepping for hasRole() calls. Example: security.rbac.role-permissions.PAYMENT_ADMIN[0]=payment:read security.rbac.role-permissions.PAYMENT_ADMIN[1]=payment:approve

properties.name: management.endpoint.security-rbac.enabled
properties.description: Whether to enable the securityRbac endpoint.
